title: Workforce runway + token-offset scenario catalog
body:
Purpose:
This working doc catalogs a compact set of budget + headcount scenarios that couple token pricing sensitivity to hiring cadence and runway. Intended as the source-of-truth for next-week finance sync and for feeding the Q4 Dedicated commercial planning workshop. Draft — please add comments inline.

High-level summary (one-line):
Map how small per-token price movements and token-mix shifts change hiring gates, runway days, and required burst reserves under three operational modes: hosted growth, dedicated conversion, and conservative enterprise-only.

Key inputs (to be mirrored in the GA spreadsheet tab 'Inputs'):
- Baseline ARR (annualized from trailing 3 months): $46.2M
- Token revenue split (gen tokens : embedding tokens : rerank) = 72% : 22% : 6%
- Effective rev per 1k gen tokens: $0.022 (baseline); embedding per 1k: $0.50
- Direct cost per 1k gen tokens (inference & infra): $0.009
- Average hiring fully-loaded cost (first-year): $210k per SWE/ML; $160k per infra/SRE; $120k per non-engineering FTE
- Average ramp (time-to-full-productivity) = 10 weeks for eng, 8 weeks infra, 6 weeks GTM
- Base monthly burn (op-ex + committed infra): $4.8M
- Burst reserve pool (current committed credits) = $6.0M
- Attrition baseline = 14% annual; shock scenario = 28% annual for 6 months
- Capital cushion target = 18 months at baseline burn

Scenario catalog (name -> what it toggles):
1) Base steady-state (S0): no price moves, token mix steady, headcount hires per plan (net +18 FTE Q4)
   - Outcome: runway ~ 18 months, cushion met, no change to pricing or commit tiers.

2) Token-down microshock (S1) : -6% yield on gen-token rev (e.g., competitors pressure / trial conversion) over Q4
   - Immediate impact: monthly rev down ~ -1.8% (mix-adjusted); hit to gross margin per token; hiring gate moves from +18 to +6 FTE for Q4.
   - Mitigation levers: tighten non-critical hiring, accelerate Optimize quantization rollouts (target 12% per-token cost savings), defer 1-month of Dedicated capacity expansion.

3) Token-up elasticity test (S2): +4% effective per-token price via tiered slab introduction for high-volume customers (pilot)
   - Revenue lift concentrated in top 20 customers; projected rev +2.2% month-over-month when fully rolled.
   - Hiring impact: allows reallocation of 6 FTE from hiring freeze pool to product and reliability work.

4) Attrition shock with price softness (S3): Attrition spike to 28% for 6 months + token yield -4%
   - Outcome: net headcount gap +33 vacancies; hiring cadence must increase to replace attrition + planned growth.
   - Cash impact: hiring acceleration increases near-term cash outflow (recruiting + ramp payroll) and reduces runway by ~2.6 months unless price lift or reserve drawdown.

5) Dedicated conversion surge (S4): 10% of hosted customers convert to dedicated/pinned capacity (three-month rollout)
   - Revenue: upfront commit credit recognized earlier (quarterly skew), but margin compression in first 6 months due to on-prem discounting and allocation of reserved GPUs.
   - Headcount: +3 infra hires immediately (to support onboarding), +2 solutions engineers per major cohort.

Decision gates and automatic triggers (proposal):
- If month-over-month effective token yield delta <= -3% for two consecutive months -> hiring gate to freeze non-essential hires and open rapid cost-savings playbook (Quantization acceleration, caching sweeps, 7-day audit on burst reservations).
- If ARR expansion > 1.5% MoM for two months with sustained gross margin > 60% -> greenlight +12 headcount for product and SRE.
- If attrition > 20% rolling 3-month annualized -> escalate to People Ops and approve a one-time retention pool ($500k) and a 6-week recruiting surge budget.

Representative mini-sheet snapshot (text table to mirror 'Outputs' tab):
Tab: Outputs (Q4 incremental)
| Scenario | Net new hires (Q4) | Runway impact (months) | Cash delta (Q4) |
| S0 Base  | +18               | +0                    | $0k             |
| S1 -6%   | +6                | -0.5                  | -$420k          |
| S2 +4%   | +24               | +1.0                  | +$1.2M          |
| S3 Attr. | +33                | -2.6                  | -$2.9M          |
| S4 Ded   | +8                | -0.8                  | +$600k (timing) |
Notes on model mechanics (important to review before stakeholder readout):
- We assume pricing moves are applied to realized tokens in the month they occur (no lag). Real customer MRC recognition and committed credit accounting will change timing of revenue; model includes credit drawdown smoothing but the Outputs table is cash-focused, not GAAP.
- Cost savings from Optimize (quantization + caching) are phased: 20% of target savings realized in month 1, 60% by month 3, rest by month 6.
- Hiring cost includes recruiting agency fees only when we do hiring acceleration (>10 roles in <60 days).

Open questions and uncertainties (please annotate):
- How should we model churn feedback loop for price increases? (Conservative: 1% churn per 3% price lift; Aggressive: 2.5%)
- Should we treat Dedicated conversion as revenue neutral over 12 months or accretive due to cross-sell? (Sales ops input required)
- What is the likely lag between Dedicated deal close and committed GPU allocation (ops dependency)?

Action items (owners):
- Evan Park: update the linked spreadsheet 'Inputs' tab with latest token telemetry (due 2026-11-04).
- Lena Thompson: run sensitivity runs for price-lift buckets +1%, +3%, +5% and post snapshots to Confluence (due 2026-11-08).
- Rahul Mehta: create recruiting surge budget line item and estimate contractor vs perm mix cost (due 2026-11-06).

Appendix: quick checklist for the Q4 finance-readout
- Bring the Google sheet 'scenario engine' with base vs S1-S4 toggles.
- One slide showing headcount phasing and cash curves for Base vs Attrition shock.
- Short note from People Ops on realistic time-to-fill for infra and SRE (we assume 10 weeks; confirm).

Questions for the readout (for execs):
- If customers accept a tiered slab for heavy gen usage, do we prefer earlier margin capture (short-term) vs long-term price floor?
- What comfort level do we have with borrowing runway (reserve drawdown) to maintain hiring momentum for mission-critical infra work?

End of draft.

Comments: this file is intentionally compact — the full workbook has the month-by-month cash waterfall and hire-by-role phasing. Link above.
